canonical.name: A vector field is a smooth section of TM, not merely a pointwise assignment of tangent vectors
Smooth vector fields and derivations of C^infty(M) are equivalent viewpoints
Pushforwards of vector fields are only asserted for diffeomorphisms, with F-relatedness as the general comparison notion
The Lie bracket is defined first as a commutator on functions, and Jacobi is proved at that operator level
The Lie bracket is not C^infty-linear in each entry
Point values X_p and Y_p do not determine the bracket value [X,Y]_p; first derivatives enter
The maximal flow has an open domain with interval fibres, and the local group law is proved from uniqueness after time shift
Completeness means all maximal integral curves are defined for all real time, and compact support is a sufficient global hypothesis
The Lie derivative of a vector field uses inverse-time pushforward so that L_XY=[X,Y]
General tensor-field and differential-form Lie derivatives are deferred to the later Cartan-calculus pages
canonical.reason: The DG-9 design fixes this page at the vector-field level. The full tensor and form versions need the tensor and exterior-form objects constructed first, so they belong to DG-11 and DG-12 rather than here.

contents.reason: This is Merry's general tensor-derivation definition. DG-9 stops at functions and vector fields because the tensor-field and exterior-form objects are owned by DG-11 and DG-12.

contents.name: Theorem 22.12
contents.reason: The extension of the Lie derivative from functions and vector fields to arbitrary tensor fields belongs after the tensor bundles themselves are built on DG-11.

contents.name: Proposition 22.14
contents.reason: Merry states the general flow formula for the Lie derivative of tensor fields here, but DG-9 only fixes the sign convention at the vector-field level. The full tensor and form flow formulas belong with Cartan calculus on DG-12.
